slides.say: A circle has a radius of root thirty-five centimeters. Its central angles are alpha and beta in turn, five of each, as in the figure. One sector with angle alpha and one sector with angle beta are shaded. What is their total area, in square centimeters?
The shaded part is part of the circle's area. So we need two things. The area of the whole circle, and which part of it is shaded.
[short pause] Let's start with the area of the circle. The radius is given, so it's easy. Pi r squared.
Root thirty-five, squared, is thirty-five, because the square cancels the root. So the area is thirty-five pi. That's the whole circle.
at: So the area is thirty-five pi

slides.say: Now, which part is shaded? We need the combined share of one alpha sector and one beta sector. We don't need either angle on its own. And that's lucky, because we don't get a number for either of them.
Let's count them. One, two, three, four, five alphas. And five betas.
All ten angles go around the center, so together they make three hundred sixty degrees. So five alpha plus five beta is three hundred sixty.
at: So five alpha plus five beta

slides: That's one equation with two unknowns. We can't find alpha or beta on its own, but we can find their sum. And the sum is all we need.

slides.say: Let's read the equation another way. The circle is made of five alpha plus beta pairs, all the same. So five times alpha plus beta is three hundred sixty. Now divide both sides by five. Alpha plus beta is seventy-two.
at: The circle is made of five alpha plus beta pairs
So five times alpha plus beta
Now divide both sides by five

slides.say: What does that tell us about alpha and beta on their own? We don't know. Alpha could be thirty and beta forty-two. Or twelve and sixty. Both pairs add up to seventy-two. There are endless options. But it doesn't matter.
The two shaded sectors are exactly one of these five equal pairs. So they're seventy-two degrees out of three hundred sixty, which is one fifth of the circle.
at: The two shaded sectors are exactly one

slides.say: So the shaded area is one fifth of thirty-five pi. Thirty-five pi divided by five is seven pi. Choice number two is our answer. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number two is our answer
